recipes.name: Smoky Chipotle Meatloaf
ingredients_raw: 2 cloves garlic, minced, or to taste
2 chipotle chilies in adobo sauce, minced, or to taste
2 tablespoons adobo sauce from chipotle peppers

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spray a 9x5-inch loaf pan with cooking spray.

Whisk eggs in a large mixing bowl until smooth. Whisk in 1/3 cup barbecue sauce, garlic, chipotle chiles, adobo sauce, kosher salt, black pepper, celery salt, cumin, and Worcestershire sauce until evenly smooth. Mix in onion, oatmeal, and ground beef with your hands until evenly blended. Pack mixture into the prepared pan. Brush the top with 2 tablespoons barbecue sauce.
Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center, about 1 hour. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Smoky Chipotle Meatloaf
raw_recipe.description: This simple chipotle meatloaf is spicy and sweet with a smoky flavor. It's delicious right out of the oven, but the leftovers make incredible sandwiches.

review.reviewBody: If you really enjoy that smokey flavor there are tons of chipotle recipes on the internet. I take a can of chipotles (undrained) and puree it until smooth. Put it in a small jar and refrigerate. This is called chipotle paste. You can add a teaspoon or so to any recipe to add that smokey taste. I use it in my chicken broth for soups, cook chicken tenders in a mixture of cream cheese and chipotle in my small crockpot, add some to ketchup or your favorite BBQ sauce, make a Denver omelette and add a little before cooking. The possibilities are endless and chipotle paste is a little addictive!

Family loved it. Here are my change: no adobo spice or celery salt around so added 1 tsp mustard powder, 1 tsp garlic powder in addition to the fresh garlic, and 1Tbs brown sugar. Mixed all ingredients then put in a casserole dish and topped loaf with approx 1Tbs BBQ sauce. I work evenings so cooked the loaf in my slow cooker by putting water in the bottom of the cooker then placing the casserole dish inside. Set for 3hours on low then on warm setting til hubby and toddler got home. Hubby broiled the loaf to crispen the top. Yummy! But why, oh why, did I agree that my husband could have the leftovers?!

It turned out well. I added a bit more adobe sauce and mixed it well. Also mixed a tablespoon of adobe sauce into the BBQ sauce topping. I put the meatloaf into three small foil loaf pans. One of which I baked, the others are frozen.

This recipe was INCREDIBLE! I followed exact recipe but was sure to split the chipotle peppers and de-seed them before chopping and putting them in meat mixture. The seeds hold more heat. Smokey, flavorful, with a small hint of kick. Savory and very slightly sweet (and I hate sweet food). Note…the added adobo sauce is key, so do not skimp. Also, separate leftover chipotles and place one or two with some sauce in each plastic snak sized bag…then label and freeze…freezes well and great to grab to flavor chili’s burgers, tacos, enchiladas, soups!

This recipe is off the hook, GOOD! A nice little zip too! I love the smokey flavor of the Chiplote peppers and adobo. I used Kraft Hickory BBQ Sauce and gave it more smokey flavor. THEN>>>Grilled the leftovers on the grill with applewood chips! OMG!!! Unbelieveable!
I left out the Chipotle peppers. Added 1/2 cup of chopped red peppers and 1 tsp. of Mesquite powder. Used Sweet Baby Rays BBQ sauce. Best I've ever had, had to save the recipe.
This is Great I made a paste of chipotle adobe peppers and ketchup put on top after it’s done. Depending on heat desired you can use more or less chipotle peppers.

Fabulous! You should definitely give it at try. I read the reviews and made it early allowing the flavors to meld. I put in a loaf pan then refrigerated for 4 hours. Inverted the loaf onto my greased broiling pan then smothered in Sweet Baby Rays BBQ sauce then topped with cracked black pepper and crushed red pepper. Roasted at 350 until done. Make a double batch if you want any leftovers :)

Really, really tasty dish. Followed recipe exactly except used 3 adobos and added some cheddar cheese to mixture. I also cooked in muffin tins instead of as loaf (cooks faster...probably 30 minutes). We also wanted it a little browned on top and so finished it under broiler for a few minutes. My husband said it is his new favorite dish I make.

I love it! I did make a few changes such as adding a couple stalks of celery (instead of the celery salt) and some carrots while cutting the onion to half. I also like my meatloaf a bit moist so added unsweetened unflavored almond milk to give it that oomph! Also, to cut the sugar (since most hickory BBQ's have at least 15g of sugar per two tablespoons!) I used a regular 4g of sugar for the loaf and added the hickory BBQ to glaze. I think next time I will do 3 peppers instead of 4 but overall it came out delicious!
Delicious! My only changes were using store bought Pico (1 c) in place of onion, replace oatmeal with 1 c corn chips and 1/2 c milk. Loved it, not to spicy!
I have made this many times and since it's just me I cut it and freeze it for lunches or dinner. I love it!!! Only change I make is to add bacon and cut the loaf to make 6 slices.
Very good! Will add more chipotle peppers next time.
This is one thing I make that my husband actually asks for. I use 1 pound of ground beef and 1 pound of ground turkey to make it SLIGHTLY healthy. Lol

Doubled the recipe. Added 3 adobo chili's with sauce, onion powder, Italian seasoning, onion powder, smoked paprika powder and 2 cups of Italian seasoning. Also used 2 lbs of lean ground beef and ground pork. Turned out yummy but a little on the "runny" side. May need to add more breadcrumbs??? Also baked it for 1 hr and 20 minutes. My family LOVED it. Definitely a keeper.
It's really good, the only change I made was instead of celery salt, I just changed it to celery and added some Chopped bell pepper. It turned out really good.
Making the recipe again! I use ground turkey for my meat choice. I also line my cooking sheet with parchment paper and mold a loaf. The meat doesn't stew and you get 3 sides crisped.

I only used 1 lb of ground beef so had to adapt. It was very flavorful but didn’t hold together like meat loaf should. My mistake. Served with baked potato and sweet potato along with steamed broccoli. Very good.
Love it! Deliciously spicy version of the usual meatloaf.
